## Audit Metadata

Who touched a record, when, and against which version of the rules: `createdBy`/`createdAt`, `lastChangedBy`/`lastChangedAt`, `changeCount`, `sourceVersion`.

```ts
import { AuditMetadataField } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/audit-metadata-field';
@field meta = contains(AuditMetadataField);
```

**`sourceVersion` is the part that is easy to omit and expensive to miss.** A result recorded in March was judged against March's rule, and a rule edited in June does not retroactively change what the auditor saw. Without it, re-reading an old report silently reinterprets it — the report says "pass" and the reader checks today's rule to find out what that meant.

`changeCount` staying at zero is itself the claim worth making on an append-only record: nothing has been rewritten since.

## Example
The contained example is the stamp on the FY26 H2 run — recorded 2026-09-07, unchanged since, rules at `supplier-controls v1`.

## Non-goals
Not the audit trail: a trail is a sequence of events on its own card (Audit Entry), this is a stamp on one record. Does not enforce immutability — it reports whether something changed, and the closing command decides what that means.
